title: Parser project fragment
description: Project-schema fragment contributed by @jxsuite/parser: the `content` section declaring file-based content collections.

content.description: File-based content collections. Each key names a content type; entries are loaded from the named source through the format registry.

additionalProperties.description: Content type definition. Defines the source, how entries are filtered, identified and routed, and their schema and element dependencies.

$elements.description: Custom elements available in markdown directives for this content type.

format.description: Name of a format class provided by an enabled extension (e.g. "Markdown", "Csv"). When omitted, the format is derived from the source file extension via the format registry. "json" is the only built-in.

schema.description: JSON Schema for validating frontmatter of content type entries.

properties.description: Field definitions; values are field schemas from the effective project field union.

required.description: Frontmatter fields every entry must provide.

source.description: Path to the content directory relative to the project root.

exclude.description: Glob patterns, relative to the source directory, for files that are never read: `internal/**`, `STYLE.md`, `**/node_modules/**`, `.*/**`. `*` and `?` stop at `/`, `**` crosses directories, `{a,b}` alternates, and dotfiles are ordinary files. A bare name with no extension (`internal`) excludes that folder as well as a file of the name. A pattern cannot climb out of the source (`../`). Excluded files are not parsed, validated, routed, linked to, searched or published, and the collection's asset mount does not serve them either: a note that refers to one gets a warning and the reference is left as written.

where.description: Declarative frontmatter filter: only entries whose frontmatter satisfies every key are kept. A value is a literal to equal (a scalar also matches an array field that contains it; an array or an object with no `$` keys is compared whole) or an operator object: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$in`, `$nin`, `$exists`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`. Keys combine with AND; there is no OR and nothing is evaluated. A filter that removes every entry is reported. Filtered entries are not validated, routed, linked to, queried or searched, and are not served from the collection's asset mount.

idField.description: Frontmatter field whose value is the entry id, instead of the path-derived id. An entry without the field keeps its path id and is reported.

route.description: A site-absolute path template. `{name}` inserts the entry id (`id`), the file's directory (`dir`), its name (`file`) or a frontmatter field (dotted paths allowed); `{name:slug}` slugifies it, and `lower`, `upper` and `raw` are also available.

indexRoute.description: The route template for a directory's `README.md` or `index.md`, the file a folder stands for, when it should differ from `route` (a section's page at `/kb/{dir:slug}/` rather than `/kb/{category:slug}/{slug}/`). It takes the same placeholders and transforms as `route`, and needs a `route` for every other entry.

links.description: How a relative link to an entry that has no page (excluded, filtered out by `where`, unrouted, or missing) is reported. The link renders as plain text in every mode. Relative links are only rewritten for content types that declare a `route`.

alerts.description: How GitHub-style alerts (`> [!NOTE]`) in Markdown entries render. `false` turns callouts off for the whole type; `true`, or leaving the option out, renders NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING and CAUTION as built-in accessible markup. An object maps an alert type (case-insensitive) to the custom element that renders it, e.g. { "NOTE": "doc-note" }; `true` renders a type with the built-in markup (how a type beyond GitHub's five, such as Obsidian's `info`, is switched on); null or false leaves a type an ordinary blockquote. A well-formed marker of a type that is not enabled is reported when the file loads.
